description.narrative: The project will provide financing to MSMEs located in Ghana.The most significant expected project-level outcome for the project is access to finance for MSMEs. Beyond the Project, this transaction is part of a programmatic approach that IFC anticipates has the potential to promote greater Competitiveness. IFCs program helps address the critical challenges in Ghana's SME finance market by demonstrating the commercial viability of new SME lending business models that serve a wide array of MSMEs.

The proposed project consists of a 5-year senior unsecured loan of up to US$20 million in USD to Access Bank Ghana (Access Ghana or the Bank) to support the provision of funding to Micro, Small, and Medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) that have been negatively impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic in Ghana (the Project). The Project will include up to US$10 million on IFCs own account and up to US$10 million in funded mobilization. Up to 30% of the aggregate loans proceeds will be earmarked to women and women-owned MSMEs, on a best-efforts basis. The Project is being processed under IFCs Base of the Pyramid (BOP) Program to support the growth of the banks MSME portfolio and will benefit from up to US$130 million Pooled First Loss Guarantee (PFLG) on the BOP Program-level provided by International Development Agency IDA Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility (IDA-PSW BFF).
